app.name: Outpost Academy
app.tagline: Every choice has a cost. See why.

common.tryAgain: Play again with a new plan

first_day.name: First Day
first_day.intro: Welcome to your Moon base! Four astronauts are counting on you.
first_day.goal: Keep the air machine running and the shield strong.
first_day.tip: Every day you get energy blocks. Share them wisely!
first_day.fact: An astronaut needs a bit less than 1 kilogram of oxygen every day.
first_day.askKid: Which system would you protect first, and why?
first_day.learn: Everything on a base runs on limited energy, so every choice has a cost.

long_night.name: Long Night
long_night.intro: Night is coming. The Sun will hide for days.
long_night.goal: Save energy in the battery before the lights go out.
long_night.tip: No sunlight means no new blocks. Plan ahead!
long_night.fact: On the Moon, one night lasts about two weeks on Earth.
long_night.askKid: How many days of energy should we save?
long_night.learn: Planning ahead: what you save today prevents problems tomorrow.

storm_watch.name: Storm Watch
storm_watch.intro: A storm of space particles may reach the base.
storm_watch.goal: Make the shield strong before the storm arrives.
storm_watch.tip: The forecast shows when the storm comes. Use it!
storm_watch.fact: NASA scientists track solar flares every day.
storm_watch.askKid: Why is it smart to prepare before the storm?
storm_watch.learn: Real space weather forecasts give crews time to prepare. Protection costs energy that you cannot use elsewhere.

green_thumb.name: Green Thumb
green_thumb.intro: Fresh food needs a garden. Time to build a greenhouse!
green_thumb.goal: Grow food without leaving the base in the dark.
green_thumb.tip: Plant lamps use energy. Balance light, air and shield.
green_thumb.fact: Astronauts on the space station have grown and eaten lettuce.
green_thumb.askKid: What would you give up for a bigger harvest?
green_thumb.learn: Growing food takes energy and water, so every system competes for the same resources.

thirsty_base.name: Thirsty Base
thirsty_base.intro: Water is the base lifeline. Time to find it and save it.
thirsty_base.goal: Share water between drinking, plants and air.
thirsty_base.tip: Mining ice costs energy. Recycling saves it.
thirsty_base.fact: Astronauts recycle most of their water, even from sweat and breath.
thirsty_base.askKid: Where does water matter most on a base?
thirsty_base.learn: Water connects all the other systems, so a shortage spreads quickly.

mars_arrival.name: Red Planet Arrival
mars_arrival.intro: Mars is far from the Sun, so sunlight is weaker than on Earth. Dust in the air makes it weaker still.
mars_arrival.goal: Keep the air running and the shield strong until the dust passes.
mars_arrival.tip: Check the Mars sky: dust means fewer energy blocks. Save energy in the battery.
mars_arrival.fact: Dust storms on Mars can grow so large that they cover the whole planet.
mars_arrival.askKid: Why does dust make a Mars base weaker?
mars_arrival.learn: Solar panels need sunlight. Dust blocks the light, so crews must save energy and sometimes clean the panels.

mars_dust_season.name: Dust Storm Season
mars_dust_season.intro: Three dusty days are coming. The sky turns orange and the panels get almost no light.
mars_dust_season.goal: Survive three dusty days without losing hearts.
mars_dust_season.tip: Fill the battery before the dust arrives, then spend it slowly.
mars_dust_season.fact: In 2018 a dust storm covered the whole of Mars. NASA's solar-powered Opportunity rover went silent.
mars_dust_season.askKid: How can a crew prepare for days without sunlight?
mars_dust_season.learn: Dust storms can last for weeks. Crews plan for them by storing power and cleaning the panels.

mars_red_garden.name: Red Garden
mars_red_garden.intro: Mars has no strong magnetic shield, so radiation reaches the ground. The crew also needs food.
mars_red_garden.goal: Grow food, keep the shield strong and keep every heart.
mars_red_garden.tip: Plants need energy too. Do not forget the shield when a storm is coming.
mars_red_garden.fact: MOXIE, a small machine on Perseverance, made oxygen from Martian air.
mars_red_garden.askKid: Why do Mars bases need a radiation shield?
mars_red_garden.learn: Mars has no global magnetic field, so particles from the Sun reach the surface. A base needs shielding, and shielding costs energy.

battery_full_wasted.title: The battery was full
battery_full_wasted.why: Extra energy was lost. Next time, use it or save it.

dust_cut_power.title: Dust covered the panels
dust_cut_power.why: Dust blocks sunlight, so the base got less energy.

water_short.title: Water ran low
water_short.why: Without enough water, other systems slowed down.

air_short.title: The air machine lacked energy
air_short.why: It needs 2 blocks each day to make fresh air.

science_air_cost.title: A science walk used air
science_air_cost.why: Going outside costs air, so plan it carefully.

food_short.title: Food ran out
food_short.why: The crew got weak without food.

air_empty.title: The air ran out
air_empty.why: Without fresh air the crew lost a heart.

micro_hit.title: A space rock hit the shield
micro_hit.why: Tiny rocks can damage the shield, so keep it strong.

storm_weak_shield.title: The shield was too weak
storm_weak_shield.why: A weak shield lets space particles reach the crew.

storm_ok.title: The shield held
storm_ok.why: Strong shielding kept the crew safe.

clean_air_cost.title: Cleaning the panels used air
clean_air_cost.why: Going outside to clean costs air, but it gives more energy tomorrow.

decision_airlock.title: Mission Control decision: air filters
decision_airlock.why: You chose between fresher air and saving energy.

decision_patch.title: Mission Control decision: the shield crack
decision_patch.why: You chose between a stronger shield and new science.

decision_rest.title: Mission Control decision: tired crew
decision_rest.why: You chose between rest and an extra energy block.

decision_solar.title: Mission Control decision: dusty panels
decision_solar.why: You chose between more energy tomorrow and saving air.

drone_used.title: The scout drone explored
drone_used.why: The drone did the science, so nobody had to go outside and breathe extra air.

radio_used.title: You called Earth
radio_used.why: Earth helped the weakest system, but the call used a block of energy.

radio_sent.title: You called Earth (the answer is on its way)
radio_sent.why: A message from Mars needs minutes to reach Earth, and the answer needs minutes to come back. So Earth's help arrives next sol, not now.

radio_arrived.title: Earth's answer arrived
radio_arrived.why: Yesterday's call was answered: Earth helped your weakest system. Planning ahead matters when help is slow.

howTo.title: How to play
howTo.s1: Look at the yellow squares: that is your energy for today.
howTo.s2: Tap + on a machine to give it energy. The Air machine always needs 2.
howTo.s3: Press End day. Watch the hearts: they show if your crew is safe.

together.title: Co-pilot corner
together.what: A grown-up and a child play as a team. The child taps the blocks (Pilot). The grown-up reads the clues and asks questions (Co-pilot).
together.roles: Pilot: the child taps + and −. Co-pilot: the grown-up reads aloud and asks.

q.air: Ask: What happens if the air machine does not get its 2 blocks?
q.waste: Ask: Why is it a pity to waste energy blocks? Where could they go instead?
q.storm: Ask: The storm comes tomorrow. How strong should the shield be, and why?
q.micro: Ask: What could a space rock do to the shield? How can you get ready?
q.ok: Ask: What do you think will happen when you press End day? Say your guess, then check the report.

together.after: Talk about it: What surprised you? What will you change tomorrow?
together.debrief: Talk about it: What would you do differently next time?

facts.title: Did you know?
facts.oxygen: One astronaut breathes almost 1 kilogram of oxygen every day.
facts.flare: Solar flares are ranked A, B, C, M and X. Each letter is about 10 times stronger than the one before.
facts.moxie: A small machine on Mars called MOXIE made oxygen from the Martian air.
facts.delay: A radio message from Mars to Earth can take up to about 20 minutes.
facts.sol: One day on Mars, called a sol, lasts about 24 hours and 40 minutes.
facts.marsdust: Dust storms on Mars can grow so large that they cover the whole planet.
facts.bones: In space, astronauts' bones and muscles can get weaker, so they exercise every day. NASA keeps this science in a free open library called OSDR.
facts.radlab: Instruments on the International Space Station measure radiation all the time. NASA shares these real measurements in a public database called RadLab.
facts.trek: NASA Mars Trek is a free website with real maps and heights of Mars, made from NASA missions. Anyone can use it to look for a place to land.
facts.csafood: Growing food on the Moon could feed astronauts, and the same ideas can help people who live far away from shops on Earth.
